skills.name: The coordinate plane: ordered pair, abscissa, ordinate, origin

note.text:
A coordinate plane has two number lines that are perpendicular: the horizontal x-axis and the vertical y-axis. They cross at the origin, O.
Every point has two coordinates, written as an ordered pair (x, y):
• the first number, x, is the abscissa: how far to go right (positive) or left (negative) from O;
• the second number, y, is the ordinate: how far to go up (positive) or down (negative).
The origin is O(0, 0). The order matters: (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points.
A point on the x-axis has ordinate 0, for example (4, 0). A point on the y-axis has abscissa 0, for example (0, −3).

worked_example.problem: Point P has coordinates {pt(x, y)}. Give its abscissa and its ordinate, and say how to reach P from the origin.
steps: In an ordered pair the first number is the abscissa: {x}.
The second number is the ordinate: {y}.
From O, go {x} units to the right (the abscissa is positive), then {-y} units down (the ordinate is negative).

cards.idea: The coordinate plane has a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis. They are perpendicular and cross at the origin O.
example: The origin is the point O{pt(z, z)}.
Numbers on the x-axis grow to the right; numbers on the y-axis grow upwards.

right.text: The x-axis and the y-axis are perpendicular

wrong.explain: The origin is where the axes cross: both coordinates are 0.
The x-axis is the horizontal one.
The y-axis is the vertical one.

wrong.text: The x-axis and the y-axis are parallel
wrong.explain: The axes cross at the origin, at a right angle: they are perpendicular.

cards.idea: A point is given by an ordered pair (x, y). The first number is the abscissa; the second is the ordinate.
example: In {pt(x, y)}, the abscissa is {x} and the ordinate is {y}.

cards.idea: The order matters: swapping the two numbers gives a different point.
example: {pt(b, a)}: {b} along, {a} up. It is another point.

cards.idea: A point on the x-axis has ordinate {z}. A point on the y-axis has abscissa {z}.

questions.prompt: In the ordered pair {pt(x, y)}, what is the abscissa?

misconceptions.explain: {y} is the ordinate, the second number. The abscissa is the first number.
Keep the sign: the first number is {x}.

solution: The abscissa is the first number of the ordered pair.

questions.prompt: In the ordered pair {pt(x, y)}, what is the ordinate?

misconceptions.explain: {x} is the abscissa, the first number. The ordinate is the second number.
Keep the sign: the second number is {y}.

solution: The ordinate is the second number of the ordered pair.

questions.prompt: Where is the point {pt(k == 0 ? v : (k == 1 ? z : v), k == 0 ? z : (k == 1 ? v : w))}?
questions.correct: {k == 0 ? 'on the x-axis' : (k == 1 ? 'on the y-axis' : 'on neither axis')}

misconceptions.explain: On the x-axis the ordinate (the second number) is {z}. Here it is not.
On the y-axis the abscissa (the first number) is {z}. Here it is not.
One of the coordinates is {z}, so the point is on an axis.

solution: A point on the x-axis has ordinate {z}; a point on the y-axis has abscissa {z}.

questions.prompt: A point has abscissa {x} and ordinate {y}. Which ordered pair is it?

misconceptions.explain: Keep the sign of the abscissa: {x}.
Keep the sign of the ordinate: {y}.

solution: The abscissa comes first and the ordinate second.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.

pool.right: the first number of an ordered pair
the second number of an ordered pair
the point (0, 0), where the axes cross
two numbers in brackets, in a fixed order

wrong.explain: The abscissa is the first number, {x}.
Its ordinate is {z}, so it is on the x-axis.

wrong.text: {pt(x, y)} and {pt(y, x)} are the same point
wrong.explain: The order matters: {pt(x, y)} and {pt(y, x)} are different points.
The ordinate is the second number, {y}.
